title: Sole innerHTML sink interpolates runtime state unescaped — safe only because the counters are numeric-by-construction (no untrusted source)
evidence: surge-explainer.html:846: `  document.getElementById('r-email').innerHTML = s.del.email + "<small> del · " + s.drop.email + " drop</small>";` :847: `  document.getElementById('r-stream').innerHTML = s.del.stream + "<small> del · " + s.drop.stream + " drop</small>";` — the only DOM HTML sinks in the file; the interpolated state is initialized at :499-500 `    del: {email:0, stream:0},` / `    drop: {email:0, stream:0},` and reaches these sinks only via `++` increments (no location/URL/input/textarea/cookie/postMessage source exists anywhere in the file; single inline <script> at :463, zero external fetches).
detail: No injection path today — interpolated values are numeric counters, only ever incremented, with no untrusted source. But safety depends on data flow, not structure; this is the artifact's one unescaped HTML sink.
recommended_fix: Replace innerHTML with textContent: put the static '<small> del · … drop</small>' unit labels in markup and set only the numbers via textContent, eliminating the committed artifact's sole HTML sink.
